data.title: American Incomes Hit Record Last Year as Women Gained Ground — WSJ
data.description:
By Paul Overberg and Rachel Wolfe

A broad measure of American incomes reached a record high last year as upper-income households fared well and women's pay gained ground compared with men, according to the Census Bureau.

The annual Census report on households' financial well-being sheds light on how Americans fared during President Trump's first year back in office, but also before the war in Iran led to soaring prices at gas pumps, higher inflation and more pressure on Americans' wallets.

Median household income topped the peak hit just before the Covid-19 pandemic, reaching $87,460 in 2025, up 2.6% from 2024 after adjusting for inflation, the new data show. Upper-income households posted gains while lower-income households didn't, reflecting a growing divide where high earners are doing most of the spending.

"This is a signal that the economy may be finally finding its groove coming out of the pandemic," said Wells Fargo economist Shannon Grein. But, she noted, the gains haven't been evenly felt.

Other key findings in the report:

After two straight years where the pay gap between women and men widened, women had a good year. Women who worked full time year-round earned about 84 cents for every dollar that comparable men worked, up from about 81 cents the previous year.

Households headed by Black Americans saw the largest income gains among racial groups at 4.8%, while those of non-Hispanic whites rose 2.9%. Income gains for Hispanic and Asian households weren't significantly different.

Tuesday's report showed a mixed picture on poverty. The bureau estimated that 13.1% of the U.S. population-about 44.4 million people-lived in poverty last year, not significantly different from 2024, based on a broad measure that many economists rely on. However, the federal government's narrower official poverty measure showed 10.2% of the population was in poverty, down 0.5 percentage point from the year before.

About 26.7 million people-7.9%-lacked health-insurance coverage for the entire year, not significantly different from the previous year. Importantly, this report marks a final reading before the withdrawal of Affordable Care Act subsidies at the start of 2026 led millions to drop coverage.

The report showed that women gained financial ground as jobs within healthcare, a traditionally female-dominated industry, have grown quickly in recent years. Women have gained 765,000 jobs since December 2024, while men have lost 6,000 in the same span, according to Labor Department data.

Women's median earnings for full-time year-round work grew 3.2% from 2024 to 2025 while men didn't see a statistically significant change, the new data show.

"It's starting to feel like the beginning of a structural realignment where men are struggling more in the labor market," said Corinne Low, a labor economist at the University of Pennsylvania whose research focuses on women in the workplace.

By region, median household income in the South rose 3.4% to $80,690. Levels in the Northeast ($95,110), Midwest ($85,820) and West ($97,440) weren't significantly changed.

On poverty, Tuesday's report showed the biggest gulf in four years between two measures that the Census Bureau calculates.

Those measures tackle poverty in different ways, with the official poverty measure reflecting just pretax income. But the so-called supplemental measure-the one many economists use-includes cash income as well as noncash government aid. It also accounts for taxes paid and essential expenses like shelter, food, utilities and transportation.

The bigger gap is likely due to declines in participation in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, and increases in healthcare costs, according to University of Kentucky Center for Poverty Research director James Ziliak. New rules last year tightened eligibility for SNAP, often known as food stamps, leading to sharp reductions.

The share of those without a high school diploma who were in poverty according to the supplemental measure rose 2 percentage points between 2024 and 2025.

The bureau reported that upper-income households have resumed relative gains that slowed after the pandemic. Households at the 90th percentile of income collected $261,300, 13.1 times what households at the 10th percentile did. A decade earlier, they collected 12.2 times as much.

Write to Paul Overberg at paul.overberg@wsj.com and Rachel Wolfe at rachel.wolfe@wsj.com

data.title: Argentina submits 2027 budget bill to Congress, foresees 4% GDP growth
data.description:
Argentina's government presented its 2027 budget proposal to Congress on Tuesday, laying out President Javier Milei's economic projections and spending priorities ahead of a presidential election next year.

According to the bill, the government forecasts GDP growth of 4% in 2027 from an expected 3% this year, and expects Argentina to record a trade surplus of over $15 billion next year.

Annual inflation is projected at 18%, compared with 29% this year.

Argentina will hold presidential elections in October 2027, and Milei is widely expected to seek re-election. The budget is expected to serve as the administration's final full-year fiscal plan before the vote, and is likely to operate as a roadmap for economic and political priorities heading into the campaign.

The bill now moves to the budget committee, then to Congress. Argentina has operated for extended periods without an approved budget, with the previous year’s rolled over, which is the fallback if the process fails to secure approval.

Milei has previously said that Argentina should increase defense spending as part of a broader effort to strengthen its sovereignty claims over the Falkland Islands, known in Argentina as the Malvinas.

Milei has adopted a harder line on Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands, that Argentina calls the Malvinas after signals from U.S. President Donald Trump that Washington's longstanding neutrality on the dispute could soften.

Since taking office in late 2023, Milei has centered his economic program on spending cuts and eliminating the fiscal deficit through austerity measures that have sharply reduced public expenditure, making any proposed increase in areas such as defense particularly notable, analysts said.

data.title: Wall Street ends lower as oil spikes and the benchmark Treasury yield breaches 5%
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes down: Dow 0.63%, S&P 0.45%, Nasdaq 0.78%
  • Traders price in 94.5% chance of Fed rate hike on Wednesday
  • Dave & Buster's slides after Q2 revenue miss
  • Crypto firms sink on bitcoin weakness, US Senate not passing legislation

By Stephen Culp and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Wall Street extended its selloff on Tuesday, as rising U.S. Treasury yields, mounting debt concerns and soaring crude prices kept buyers on the sidelines.

All three major U.S. stock indexes extended Monday's losses as broad risk-off sentiment weighed on nearly every sector but energy . That sector benefited from expanding hostilities in the Middle East, which included new attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.

"Given rising prices for fuel, especially diesel, given the near-certain outlook for rising rates beginning tomorrow, and given the concerns over the potential slowdown in the AI ecosphere, why step into the market aggressively until some of this clears up?" said Peter Tuz, president of Chase Investment Counsel in Charlottesville, Virginia.

The Federal Reserve has convened for its two-day monetary policy meeting, which is due to culminate on Wednesday with the central bank's rate decision. With recent economic data showing the labor market on solid footing, while war-related energy price pressures are morphing into broader, systemic inflation, the central bank is expected to implement a 25-basis-point increase to its Fed funds target rate — its first interest rate hike in over three years.

In the wake of last week's hot inflation data and the near 25% jump in U.S. crude prices over the last two weeks, financial markets have priced in a 94.5% likelihood of a rate hike on Wednesday, up from 33.1% one month ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Tuz added that while markets will learn the Fed's decision tomorrow, "the Middle East conflict is a wild card as to how long it might last."

Front-month West Texas Intermediate and Brent oil settled up 4.4% and 2.9% respectively, while diesel futures closed at a record high.

"This will probably be not a one-and-done, but a series of rate increases," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "It will be dependent on oil; that is really the source of inflation and it's starting to seep into other parts of the market."

As rate-hike bets increased, global bond yields resumed their upward climb, with benchmark U.S. Treasury yields breaching 5% and reaching the highest level since 2007.

Rising interest rates are increasing the pressure on heavily indebted borrowers, including companies that have placed big bets on AI.

Those worries exacerbated mounting fears over AI's destructive potential and growing opposition to the construction of data centers, which came to a head on Monday and dragged the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index down.

The semiconductor index, which has helped drive broader stock market gains this year, did not meaningfully recover from Monday's rout, eking out a 0.4% gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 328.09 points, or 0.63%, to 52,093.11, the S&P 500 lost 34.25 points, or 0.45%, to 7,585.73 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 204.84 points, or 0.78%, to 25,981.57.

Among the 11 major sectors of the S&P 500, consumer discretionary stocks were the biggest percentage losers, while energy, buoyed by rising crude, advanced 2.3%.

Dave & Buster's tumbled 19% following the company's second-quarter revenue miss.

Waystar rose 7.1% after Reuters reported the healthcare software firm is exploring options, including a potential sale.

Weakness in bitcoin was compounded by the U.S. Senate not advancing comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation, in a blow to digital asset companies. Crypto firms Coinbase and Strategy dropped 10.1% and 5.4%, respectively.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.56-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 113 new highs and 673 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,439 stocks rose and 3,356 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.33-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 14 new 52-week highs and 18 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 52 new highs and 264 new lows.

Volume on U.S. exchanges was 15.85 billion shares, compared with the 15.14 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: Dow clinches its worst September start since 2008 as history repeats itself
data.description:
By Joseph Adinolfi

Tuesday is also the 18th anniversary of Lehman Brothers' bankruptcy filing, a curious coincidence

Stocks are off to a rocky start in September.

History is repeating itself on Wall Street.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA on Tuesday clinched its worst performance during the first 10 days of September since 2008, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Both the S&P 500 SPX and Nasdaq Composite COMP posted their worst 10-day starts to the month since 2020.

In a curious coincidence, Tuesday also happened to be the 18th anniversary of the bankruptcy filing of Lehman Brothers - a pivotal development that kicked off the most acute phase of the 2008 financial crisis. The Dow finished September 2008 down 6%, before falling more than 14% that October, according to FactSet data.

That stocks have struggled so far this month shouldn't come as a surprise. September has a reputation for being the worst month of the year for major U.S. equity indexes, and the data back this up. The table below from Dow Jones Market Data shows that September has seen the worst average performance of any calendar month for the Dow, the S&P 500, the Nasdaq Composite and the small-cap Russell 2000 RUT.

It is also the only calendar month where the average performance for all four indexes is negative. The chart below features data from different time frames: For the Dow, the average figure includes every year back to 1897.

"Historically September has been a bad month, so it's no surprise that's what we're looking at," said Mark Gibbens, chief investment officer at Gibbens Capital Management, during an interview with MarketWatch.

But to be sure, the calendar alone isn't responsible for this month's stock-market rockiness. Like unhappy families, each red September has been miserable for markets in its own way. This time around, rising oil prices and bond yields, coupled with growing worries about AI, have been largely to blame, Gibbens said.

With the Federal Reserve expected to hike interest rates on Wednesday, more pain for stocks could be ahead.

"On the one hand, we still have a relatively resilient labor backdrop, so consumers are benefiting from income growth month to month... but I don't want to discount the weakness associated with a potential hawkish turn by the Fed, higher rates at the long end and higher gas prices," said Kevin Gordon, head of macro research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

"To me, that all adds up to headwinds for risk assets - not necessarily winds that are strong enough to end the bull market, but certainly strong enough to engineer a bigger wave of volatility."

Stocks also struggled in September 2020, September 2021 and September 2022. In September 2020, stocks moved lower after a torrid summer rebound rally that saw major indexes claw back their COVID-19-related losses. U.S.-China tensions and worries about a COVID stimulus package that had stalled in Congress were largely to blame. In 2021, the arrival of new COVID variants and signs of a weakening Chinese economy helped send stocks lower after another exuberant stretch.

In 2022, investors reacted to then-Fed Chair Jerome Powell's warnings in a speech in Jackson Hole, Wyo., that households and businesses in the U.S. might experience some pain in the short term as he promised the central bank would continue with aggressive interest-rate hikes to tamp down inflation. Earlier in the summer, consumer-price inflation had reached its highest rate in 40 years.

Ken Jimenez contributed

-Joseph Adinolfi

data.title: Charter Declares Quarterly Cash Dividend on Series A Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock
data.description:
STAMFORD, Conn., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Charter Communications, Inc. (, CHTRP) (the "Company") today announced that its Board of Directors declared the regular quarterly cash dividend payable to holders of its Series A Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock (the "Charter Preferred Stock") (). The per share amount of the quarterly cash dividend will be $0.43750001, payable in cash on October 15, 2026 to holders of record of the Charter Preferred Stock at the close of business on September 30, 2026.

As previously disclosed, 7,183,812 shares of Charter Preferred Stock were issued in connection with the acquisition of Liberty Broadband Corporation ("Liberty Broadband"). At the effective time of the acquisition, each share of Liberty Broadband Series A Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock was converted into one newly issued share of Charter Preferred Stock. The Charter Preferred Stock is entitled to 1/3 of a vote per share, has a liquidation preference of $25 per share plus accrued but unpaid dividends, pays dividends quarterly at a 7% annual rate, and is mandatorily redeemable on March 9, 2039.

About CharterCharter Communications, Inc. (, CHTRP) is the leading broadband and video company in the nation and the fastest growing mobile provider in its footprint, with services available to more than 70 million homes and small to large businesses across 45 states through its Spectrum brand. Founded in 1993, Charter has evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience. Over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by our 100% U.S.-based employees, the Company offers Seamless Connectivity and Entertainment with Spectrum Internet®, Mobile, TV and Voice products.

More information can be found at corporate.charter.com.

SOURCE Charter Communications, Inc.

data.title: BKV Completes Acquisition of Barnett Shale Upstream, Midstream, and Carbon Capture Assets
data.description:
BKV Corporation (“BKV” or the “Company”) (NYSE: BKV) today announced it has completed the acquisition of certain Barnett Shale upstream, midstream and CCS assets. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

The acquisition further advances BKV’s closed-loop energy strategy by expanding BKV’s operational footprint and production capacity with additional high-quality, low-decline Barnett Shale assets that complement the Company’s existing operations and infrastructure. The assets strengthen BKV’s platform across natural gas upstream, midstream and carbon capture, while reinforcing its leadership position in the Barnett Shale. The transaction is expected to enhance operational and capital efficiencies through greater scale and shared infrastructure, while expanding BKV’s Barnett gas volumes available to serve demand centers in Dallas-Fort Worth and the Gulf Coast.

“These assets are a strong operational fit for BKV, and the acquisition builds on our disciplined approach to strengthening our position in the Barnett, adding low-decline production and reserves that integrate seamlessly with our existing operations and infrastructure,” said Chris Kalnin, Chief Executive Officer of BKV Corporation. “By acquiring high-quality assets at an attractive value and further integrating upstream, midstream and carbon capture in a basin where we are already the leader, we are creating additional scale and long-term value for our shareholders.”

Transaction Highlights:

  • Over 65 MMcfe/d of production, more than 50% of which is liquids, with a low PDP decline rate
  • Approximately 0.35 Tcfe of PDP reserves
  • Approximately 117,000 net acres, primarily in Montague County
  • Approximately 1,000 gross operated wells
  • An operated CCS project that has captured over 100,000 metric tons of CO2 over the trailing twelve months through the first quarter of 2026, from three compressors and a gas plant, including an operated CO2 pipeline and injection well
  • Operated midstream, including a gas plant with 180 MMcf/d of capacity and approximately 340 miles of owned gas gathering lines, plus approximately 225 miles of owned water gathering system and two saltwater disposal wells

Transaction Details

The acquisition closed on September 15, 2026, following the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. The transaction was funded through cash on hand and borrowings under the Company’s revolving credit facility.

About BKV Corporation

BKV Corporation (NYSE: BKV) is a forward-thinking, growth-driven energy company focused on the sustainable development and delivery of low-carbon energy solutions and baseload power. As the largest natural gas producer by gross operated volume in the Barnett Shale, BKV is strategically expanding an end-to-end value chain that leverages its assets in upstream production, midstream infrastructure, natural gas-fired power generation and carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS). Through this innovative, closed-loop approach, BKV solves customers’ toughest energy challenges, meeting growing power demand and enabling sustainable growth for the future. Headquartered in Denver, Colorado, BKV is committed to driving long-term, risk adjusted shareholder value by optimizing and scaling our closed-loop energy platform for a carbon neutral future. data.title: Michael Wekerle Announces Updated Holdings In Orion Digital Corp.
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

September 15, 2026 (Toronto, Ontario) – TheNewswire - Michael Wekerle (the “Acquiror”) announces updated holdings in Orion Digital Corp. (NASDAQ: ORIO; TSX: ORIO) (“Orion”) and corrections to his early warning report and related news release dated May 12, 2026. Through Wek Corp., the Acquiror acquired control or direction over an aggregate of 441,900 common shares of Orion (the “Common Shares”) at a weighted average price of approximately C$1.4208 per Common Share for aggregate consideration of approximately C$627,845.20 (the “Acquisitions”).

The Acquisitions were completed on August 28, 2026, and September 11, 2026, over the facilities of the Toronto Stock Exchange and certain alternative markets where the Common Shares are posted for trading.

Immediately prior to completion of the Acquisitions, the Acquiror beneficially owned, or exercised control or direction over, 2,503,270 Common Shares, representing approximately 10.53% of the issued and outstanding Common Shares on a non-diluted basis. Immediately following completion of the Acquisitions, the Acquiror beneficially owned, or exercised control or direction over, 2,945,170 Common Shares, representing approximately 12.38% on the same basis, an increase of approximately 1.85%. These percentages are based on 23,781,198 Common Shares outstanding as of June 30, 2026, as disclosed in Orion’s interim financial statements for that period.

The Acquiror’s early warning report and related news release dated May 12, 2026 reported holdings following purchases on May 6 and 7, 2026 of 2,420,959 Common Shares, or approximately 10.13% on a non-diluted basis. Following a reconciliation across registered holders and brokerage accounts, the corrected holdings following those purchases were 2,347,959 Common Shares, or approximately 9.83% on a non-diluted basis. Based on such corrected historical Common Share balance, the Acquiror’s ownership in the Common Shares following the Acquisitions represents a change of greater than 2% on a non-diluted basis since the acquisitions completed on May 6 and 7, 2026. Further details of the historical corrections are set out in the early warning report to be filed in connection with this news release.

The Common Shares were acquired for investment purposes. The Acquiror may acquire additional securities of Orion, including on the open market or through private acquisitions, or sell securities of Orion, including on the open market or through private dispositions, in the future depending on market conditions, reformulation of plans and/or other relevant factors. The Acquiror currently has no other plans or intentions that relate to or would result in the matters listed in clauses (b) to (k) of Item 5 of the early warning report to be filed by the Acquiror in connection with this news release. Depending on market conditions, general economic and industry conditions, Orion’s business and financial condition and/or other relevant factors, the Acquiror may develop such plans or intentions in the future.

An early warning report correcting the prior disclosure and reporting the updated holdings described above will be filed under Orion’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. A copy may also be obtained by contacting the Acquiror at the address below.

data.title: JPMorgan Expects Third-Quarter Gains in Investment Banking, Markets — WSJ
data.description:
By Jasmine Li

JPMorgan Chase is expecting growth in the "mid- to high-teens" for both investment-banking fees and markets revenue in the third quarter compared with the year-ago period, co-president Doug Petno said Tuesday.

  • "In investment banking...we started the year with a strong pipeline, we started this quarter with a strong pipeline," Petno said at a financial services conference hosted by Barclays. "And that continues."
  • Petno said the bank, which is due to report third-quarter earnings on Oct. 13, is expecting lower markets revenue compared with its record-setting second quarter.

Bank of America shares fell Monday after CEO Brian Moynihan said investment-banking revenue would fall by 10% in the quarter from a year earlier. Citigroup said it is expecting revenue growth around "low single digits" in its investment-banking business.

Asked to comment on his competitors' performance, JPMorgan's Petno said: "Not much that I want to say in this room."

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
